prompt.context: Nica Productions is an American media company trying to figure out its next project. The company has extensive experience producing series and movies for all types of audiences and has won many awards. The company has two alternatives: produce a series for a streaming company, or produce a movie to be projected in cinemas worldwide. Producing media content implies big investments and low certainty about potential incomes, which depends on many factors. The client has hired us to help decide which is the best alternative.
prompt.question: Which project should Nica Productions choose — the movie or the series — and why? Evaluate the financial attractiveness of each alternative and provide a recommendation.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profitability goal?
clarifying_info.a: No, there is no specific profitability goal.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have access to top talent?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the company is known worldwide with access to top star directors, actors, and technical staff.
No, there is no budget limitation.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the target customers for each alternative?
clarifying_info.a: Both alternatives look for worldwide reach but target different types of customers.
Production of any alternative will last one year.
No, there is no alternative project.

clarifying_info.q: What is the main revenue driver?
clarifying_info.a: The main source of revenue for both projects depends on audience size.

exhibits.title: Movies Alternative 2 — Additional Cash Flows
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing annual cash flows for Movie Alternative 2 (Michael Bay) over approximately 10 years, representing merchandising and other income streams
exhibits.data: Year 0: 20.00M, Year 1: 18.00M, Year 2: 16.20M, Year 3: 14.58M, Year 4: 13.12M, Year 5: 11.81M, Year 6: 10.63M, Year 7: 9.57M, Year 8: 8.61M, Year 9: 7.75M, Year 10: 4.58M (approximate); values decline over time

framework: Identify decision criterion: choose the project with higher positive NPV
For each alternative, estimate expected Cash Flows (investment at Year 0, income at end of Year 1)
Apply discount rate to calculate NPV for each scenario
Use probability-weighted average NPV to account for uncertainty
Consider qualitative factors: risk, competition, market trends, company strategy
Account for sunk costs correctly (series script already purchased = sunk cost)
Check for additional revenue streams (merchandising, DVD, etc.)
Deliver a structured recommendation highlighting uncertainty

questions.prompt: Calculate the NPV of the Movie alternative using Exhibit 1. Which movie director alternative yields higher expected NPV?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a decision tree. For each director alternative, compute expected audience using probability weights, then compute income, subtract investment, discount at 20%, and compare probability-weighted NPV across the two director alternatives.

math.setup: Expected audience = (Audience_Good * P_Good) + (Audience_Bad * P_Bad). Income = Total Audience * Ticket Price * Commission%. NPV = -Investment + Income / (1 + 0.20). Then weight NPV of each director alternative by its probability (60% Nolan, 40% Bay).
math.answer: Expected NPV of Movie alternative = 260M USD

questions.prompt: Calculate the NPV of the Series alternative using Exhibit 2. Be careful about which costs are relevant.
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize that the script (10M USD) is a sunk cost and should be excluded. Only the incremental investment of 100M USD (Actors + Production) plus the upfront income matters. Candidate computes expected total audience across all episodes, then calculates income, and applies the discount rate.

math.setup: Sunk cost: Script 10M USD — do NOT include. Investment = Actors (60M) + Production (40M) = 100M USD. Upfront income at Year 0 = 20M USD. Net outflow Year 0 = -100M + 20M = -80M. Expected audience per episode = (100M*30%) + (70M*40%) + (40M*30%). Total audience = Expected per episode * 10 episodes. Income Year 1 = Total Audience * 600,000 USD/PMV.
steps: Expected audience per episode = (100M*30%) + (70M*40%) + (40M*30%) = 30M + 28M + 12M = 70M per episode
If candidate mistakenly includes sunk cost: NPV = -90 + 350 = 260M USD (same as movies — error matters)
math.answer: Series NPV (correct, excluding sunk cost) = 270M USD; Series NPV (incorrect, including sunk cost) = 260M USD

questions.prompt: Exhibit 3 shows additional cash flows from merchandising and other income for Movie Alternative 2 (Bay). Does this change the recommendation?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the declining trend as a CAGR of -10% and calculate a declining perpetuity. The perpetuity formula for a growing/declining perpetuity is NPV = CF1 / (r - g), where g = -10% and r = 20%. This adds NPV to Alternative 2's base NPV, changing the weighted average movie NPV.

math.setup: Perpetuity with declining cash flows: NPV = CF_initial / (r - g) = 20M / (0.20 - (-0.10)) = 20M / 0.30. This perpetuity NPV applies only to Alternative 2. Recalculate weighted movie NPV: Alt 1 NPV stays 300M, Alt 2 NPV = 200M + 66.7M = 266.6M. Expected Movie NPV = (300M * 60%) + (266.6M * 40%).
steps: Identify CAGR: 18/20 = 0.9, so growth rate g = -10%
Movie NPV (287M) now exceeds Series NPV (270M) — recommendation flips to Movie
math.answer: With merchandising, expected Movie NPV ≈ 287M USD vs. Series NPV = 270M USD; the decision changes to choosing the Movie alternative

recommendation: Based on NPV analysis, the Series (270M USD) edges out the Movie (260M USD) when only considering base financials — but this reverses to Movie (287M USD) once merchandising cash flows for Alternative 2 are included
Recommend pursuing the Movie alternative (specifically Christopher Nolan / Alt 1 approach given its higher NPV of 300M), subject to securing the director and cast
Highlight that the decision hinges heavily on probability assumptions about audience reception and the ability to hire desired talent
risks: High uncertainty in audience projections — probability assumptions are estimates and actual performance could vary significantly
Risk that preferred director/actor (Nolan, Hardy) cannot be hired, forcing the Bay alternative with lower base NPV
Production delay risk — if the one-year production timeline slips, the launch window and projected audience may be missed
Competitive risk — a rival studio releasing a blockbuster at the same time could significantly reduce audience
Macroeconomic risk — economic downturn reducing consumer discretionary spending on entertainment
For the series: streaming platform dependency means renegotiation or platform decline could affect royalties
next_steps: Negotiate and lock in preferred director and talent as early as possible to secure Alt 1
Conduct deeper market research to validate audience size assumptions for each alternative
Stress-test NPV model under pessimistic scenarios (all Bad outcomes) to understand downside exposure
Explore ways to diversify revenue (e.g., pre-selling international rights) to reduce uncertainty
Set clear go/no-go milestones tied to talent acquisition and script development progress
